clue.text: The American's

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'The American's (8)': cut short after two words, so neither definition nor wordplay for the wallet sense survives; no scan or reprint gives the rest.

clue.text: Sternly supported?

parts.note: a ship's stern is its rear, so being supported from behind, at the back, is support given 'sternly'

explanation.surface: Someone held up by a strict, severe patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sternly' looks like 'severely', but it is read as 'at the stern', i.e. from the rear; to be supported from behind is to be given backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To have backing is to have support, literally from behind.

clue.text: Victorian who fought to keep infection out of the theatre

definitions.text: Victorian who fought to keep infection out of the theatre

parts.words: Victorian who fought to keep infection out of the theatre
parts.note: the theatre is the operating theatre, and the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery there is meant

explanation.surface: A nineteenth-century campaigner keeps disease away from stage audiences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' suggests a playhouse, but it is the hospital operating theatre: Joseph Lister introduced carbolic-acid antisepsis to surgery in the 1860s.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Lister, the Victorian surgeon, pioneered antiseptic methods in surgery.

clue.text: Small boy climbing underneath a marsh plant

indicators.note: in a down clue the reversed name goes below the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is a marsh

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the boy's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Len is a short boy's name, a diminutive of Leonard

explanation.surface: A little lad scrambles about under a waterlogged plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses LEN to NEL in this down clue, and 'underneath' puts it below FEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aromatic umbelliferous herb, a plant grown for its seeds and bulb.

clue.text: Uplifting experience of a spiritual character

definitions.text: Uplifting experience of a spiritual character

parts.words: Uplifting experience of a spiritual character
parts.note: uplifting is taken literally, a rising into the air, as reported at spiritualist seances

explanation.surface: A morale-boosting religious experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uplifting' reads as 'inspiring', but here it means physically raised: spiritualist mediums claimed to rise off the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising into the air by supposed supernatural power is a classic seance phenomenon.

clue.text: I change no gem for this Shakespeare heroine

indicators.note: the solver is told to change, that is rearrange, the letters of I and no gem

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to swap a jewel for a heroine of the Bard.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue lost its opening 'I'; 'change' rearranges I plus NOGEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is the heroine of Shakespeare's play Cymbeline.

clue.text: Give the wrong price for the shares?

definitions.text: Give the wrong price for the shares?

parts.words: Give the wrong price for the shares
parts.note: a quote is a stated price for stocks, so giving a wrong one is quoting badly, here in the sense of a stray citation

explanation.surface: A stockbroker states an incorrect share price.
explanation.walkthrough: A quotation is a price for shares on the stock market; to quote one wrongly is to get the quotation wrong, the usual sense being citing words inaccurately.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation is a stated price, so a wrong price is a faulty quotation.

clue.text: An age of moral rectitude — not what one should expect to get in it!

definitions.text: An age of moral rectitude — not what one should expect to get in it!

parts.words: An age of moral rectitude — not what one should expect to get in it
parts.note: an age of virtue is literally a virtuous period, but enjoyment of fun is hardly what such a virtuous era offers

explanation.surface: A remark that a virtuous era is no place for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, a 'good' 'time' is an age of moral rectitude; the everyday phrase means fun and pleasure, which a strictly moral era is unlikely to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase splits as virtuous plus era, while its idiom means a spell of pleasure.

clue.text: A music-box into which one's pocket-money may go?

definitions.text: A music-box into which one's pocket-money may go?

parts.words: A music-box into which one's pocket-money may go
parts.note: a container for musical notes would literally be a box for notes, but the notes are banknotes kept in a pocket wallet

explanation.surface: A child's musical box doubling as a money box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music-box' suggests a toy, but read as a case for notes it is a wallet for banknotes, where one's pocket money goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet for paper money holds banknotes, so it is a case for notes.

clue.text: A lover of Italy as described by one of his country's sculptors

indicators.note: to be described by something is to have it drawn round you, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Antonio Canova was an Italian neoclassical sculptor
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian romantic portrayed by a fellow countryman's sculpture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' signals a container: to describe a shape is to draw a line round it, as a circle is described.
explanation.definitionFit: Giacomo Casanova was the Venetian adventurer famed as a seducer and lover.

clue.text: Protection money may have to be paid to get it

definitions.text: Protection money may have to be paid to get it

parts.words: Protection money may have to be paid to get it
parts.note: protection money suggests racketeering, but here one pays a bodyguard or companion for safety

explanation.surface: A racketeer demands payment for keeping a business safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protection money' suggests extortion, but read plainly it is money paid for a protector, a guard who accompanies you.
explanation.definitionFit: A guard or companion hired to accompany someone gives protection for a fee.

clue.text: The weather men clad in processed steel

indicators.note: men clad in something are wrapped by it, so one piece sits inside the other
processed metal has been worked over, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers in worked steel armour facing the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'processed' rearranges the steel into ELETS, and 'clad in' wraps that round the men; 'The weather' wants to be a subject, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure to wind and rain is exposure to the forces of nature, which is what braving the elements means.

clue.text: A yokel in charge of incipient corrosion?

parts.note: rust is the corrosion that starts on iron and steel

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin is put in charge of preventing rust.
explanation.walkthrough: IC for 'in charge' is a standard abbreviation, placed after RUST.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustic is a country person, an unsophisticated rural type.

clue.text: Spot cash that may be put on horses?

definitions.text: that may be put on horses?

parts.note: a spot is a place
cash is money

explanation.surface: Ready money staked on racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: A place bet pays if the horse finishes in the first few, so the stake is money on a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A stake on a horse to be placed is a bet backing a top-three finish.

clue.text: It's smashed with a mallet on every conceivable occasion

indicators.note: something smashed is broken to bits, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of it's, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Something is broken with a mallet again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' rearranges ITS plus AMALLET.
explanation.definitionFit: Always, without exception, on any occasion one might think of.

clue.text: Curious I roasted a starfish

indicators.note: curious means odd, so the letters are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: An odd confession of having cooked a starfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curious' rearranges IROASTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Starfish belong to the class Asteroidea, and an individual one may be called by that class name.

clue.text: Sublime joke I found in a waterproof garment

indicators.note: something found in a garment sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
a jest is a joke

explanation.surface: A comic finds a superb gag tucked in a raincoat pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' signals a container; a mac is the everyday British word for a raincoat, short for mackintosh.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means grand or awe-inspiring, which is what sublime describes.

clue.text: Rising place in Provence with a railway and a theological college

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the town name is read from the bottom up

parts.note: Nimes is a city in southern France near Provence

explanation.surface: A town in southern France has a railway and a college for priests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses NIMES to SEMIN in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminary is a college that trains priests or ministers.

clue.text: A teacher of drama defining old world diligence?

definitions.meaning: someone who coaches actors for the stage
a diligence was a public horse-drawn coach in old Europe, especially France

explanation.surface: A drama tutor defines hard work in old-fashioned terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diligence' looks like hard work but is the French public coach of horse-drawn days.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach for the stage teaches acting, and a horse-drawn public coach was a diligence in France.

clue.text: Light machine-gun company brought into a town in Powys

indicators.note: one piece is brought into, put inside, the other

parts.note: the Bren was a British light machine-gun

explanation.surface: Soldiers carry their weapon into a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought into' signals a container; the Bren was the British army's light machine-gun of the mid-twentieth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Brecon is a market town in the Welsh county of Powys.

clue.text: Momentous races?

parts.note: races are sporting contests, and momentous happenings are significant occurrences; one word covers both

explanation.surface: Important sporting contests.
explanation.walkthrough: Athletics races are called by the same word used for important happenings in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Contests in a sports meeting and significant occurrences share one name.

clue.text: A slide from them is all too evident in the permissive society

definitions.text: A slide from them is all too evident in the permissive society

parts.words: A slide from them is all too evident in the permissive society
parts.note: a permissive society is one that has slipped away from its standards, moral goals once held high

explanation.surface: A complaint that loose modern society has fallen from its principles.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening words 'A slide' hold the same letters as the answer, a nudge rather than a signalled anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Principles and high standards are what a permissive society is said to have slipped from.

clue.text: A prescription for sickness

parts.note: a prescription is usually a cure, but this medicine is prescribed to cause vomiting

explanation.surface: A doctor's remedy for illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sickness' suggests a cure, but the drug is given to produce sickness, i.e. to make a patient vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug that induces vomiting is prescribed to bring on sickness rather than cure it.

clue.text: I'm put to the test and made better

parts.note: the letters of I'm, without the apostrophe
proved can mean tested, as in proving a gun

explanation.surface: Someone tested comes out the better for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proved' in its older sense of tested survives in 'the exception proves the rule'.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something is to make it better.

clue.text: Society offers him no legal status

definitions.text: Society offers him no legal status

parts.words: Society offers him no legal status
parts.note: a person placed beyond the protection of the law has no rights in society

explanation.surface: A man is denied rights by the community.
explanation.walkthrough: Historically such a person was put outside the law's protection entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive declared beyond the law's protection has no legal standing.

clue.text: Serpentine swimmer — the greatest of them all?

definitions.text: Serpentine swimmer — the greatest of them all?

parts.words: Serpentine swimmer — the greatest of them all
parts.note: the Serpentine is a lake in Hyde Park, but serpentine here means snake-like; the swimmer is the heaviest snake

explanation.surface: A champion swimmer in London's Serpentine lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is a lake in London's Hyde Park where swimmers race; here it means snake-like, and the green anaconda is the largest, water-loving snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The green anaconda, an aquatic South American snake, is the heaviest snake in the world.

clue.text: Alluring birds, real or artificial

parts.note: birds that lure others, whether live or wooden models, used by wildfowlers

explanation.surface: Attractive birds, some genuine and some fake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alluring' suggests attractive, but it means luring: hunters use live or carved birds to draw wildfowl within range.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildfowlers set out live or model birds to lure others within shot.

clue.text: His pony's distractedly comatose state

indicators.note: something done distractedly is done in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of his pony's, with the s kept

explanation.surface: A man's horse is in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distractedly' rearranges HISPONYS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trance-like sleep induced by suggestion resembles a comatose state.
